traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 1, 1919, pp. 44 to 46), as their subgenus Cylindropuntia of Opuntia, now a genus: joints all terete, never flattened, on plants of several many-jointed branches; the North American series (the three species here among them) have papery spine sheaths; the joints are tubercled, the tubercles long in some series, broad and low in others.
